# Results

## ILINet development: timing feature sets

```{r ili-sets}
tim_map <- c("gbqr" = "core", "gbqr__sb" = "SB", "gbqr__R1" = "SB (reported-at-t)", "gbqr__R2" = "core + B",
             "gbqr__R3" = "core + lat/lon", "gbqr__R4" = "core + recession", "gbqr__R5" = "core + holiday",
             "gbqr__R6" = "core + B + lat/lon + rec. + hol.", "gbqr__R7" = "SB + B", "gbqr__R8" = "SB + lat/lon + rec.",
             "gbqr__R9" = "SB + B + lat/lon + rec.", "gbqr__R10" = "SB + B + lat/lon + rec. + hol.")
siz_map <- c("gbqr" = "core", "gbqr__sb" = "SB", "gbqr__R1" = "SB (reported-at-t)", "gbqr__R2" = "SB + offset",
             "gbqr__R3" = "SB + B", "gbqr__R4" = "SB + trend", "gbqr__R5" = "SB + H3", "gbqr__R6" = "SB + recession",
             "gbqr__R7" = "SB + lat/lon", "gbqr__R8" = "SB + B + offset", "gbqr__R9" = "SB + trend + B",
             "gbqr__R10" = "core + offset")
ir <- ili |> filter(agg_level == "state", grepl("@rtrev$", model)) |> mutate(run = sub("@rtrev$", "", model),
                                                                            neg_log_score = -log_score) |>
  filter(run %in% c(names(tim_map), "baseline"))
dot_sets <- function(d, map, metric, xlab, title, highlight = NULL) {
  s <- d |> filter(run %in% names(map)) |> group_by(run, season) |> summarise(v = mean(.data[[metric]]), .groups = "drop") |>
    bind_rows(d |> filter(run %in% names(map)) |> group_by(run) |> summarise(v = mean(.data[[metric]])) |> mutate(season = "both")) |>
    mutate(set = map[run], season = factor(season, levels = c("2018/19", "2019/20", "both")))
  ord <- s |> filter(season == "both") |> arrange(desc(v)) |> pull(set)
  hl <- tibble(set = highlight, pos = match(highlight, ord))
  ggplot(s, aes(v, factor(set, levels = ord))) + geom_blank() +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = hl$pos - 0.45, ymax = hl$pos + 0.45, fill = "#fde9df") +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = hl$pos, label = "passed to NHSN test ", hjust = 1, color = "#d9531e", size = 4.5,
             fontface = "bold") +
    geom_point(aes(color = season, size = season == "both")) +
    scale_size_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 5, `FALSE` = 3), guide = "none") +
    scale_color_manual(NULL, values = c("2018/19" = "#e69f00", "2019/20" = "#56b4e9", "both" = INK)) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL, title = title,
         subtitle = "ILINet states, as-published data + revision simulation · large black dot: 2018/19 + 2019/20 pooled; small dots: each season\nshaded: passed on to the NHSN test")
}
```

```{r f-ili-timing}
#| fig-height: 6.8
dot_sets(ir, tim_map, "neg_log_score", "peak-week −log score (lower is better)",
         "Timing: core-based sets ≈ core; every SB-based timing set is worse",
         highlight = c("core", "core + holiday", "core + B + lat/lon + rec. + hol."))
```

::: notes
ILINet 2018/19 + 2019/20, as-published data + revision simulation, ~45 states, 29 reference dates per season. Each run fits separate size and timing models, so the timing scores depend only on the timing feature set (verified: identical forecasts across runs with the same timing set). Baseline: −log score `r f2(-mean(ir$log_score[ir$run == "baseline"]), 3)`.
:::

## ILINet development: size feature sets

```{r f-ili-size}
#| fig-height: 6.8
dot_sets(ir, siz_map, "wis_log", "peak-size log-WIS (lower is better)",
         "Size: SB best (tied with SB + lat/lon); the baseline offset clearly hurts",
         highlight = c("SB", "SB + lat/lon", "SB + B"))
```

::: small
**core** was also carried to the NHSN test, as the reference set without SB.
:::

::: notes
ILINet 2018/19 + 2019/20 pooled and by season. Baseline log-WIS `r f2(mean(ir$wis_log[ir$run == "baseline"]), 3)`. Chosen configuration from ILINet: size SB, timing core.
:::

## NHSN test: choosing the final feature sets

```{r f-nhsn-test}
#| fig-height: 6.4
# NHSN hindcasts of the sets passed on from ILINet (2023/24 + 2024/25). Size and timing models are fitted separately,
# so each run scores one size set and one timing set
nt_tim <- c("UMass-peak_gbqr__N1" = "core", "UMass-peak_gbqr__N2" = "core + holiday",
            "UMass-peak_gbqr__N3" = "core + B + lat/lon + rec. + hol.", "UMass-peak_baseline" = "baseline")
nt_siz <- c("UMass-peak_gbqr__N1" = "SB", "UMass-peak_gbqr__N2" = "SB + lat/lon", "UMass-peak_gbqr__N3" = "SB + B",
            "UMass-peak_gbqr" = "core", "UMass-peak_baseline" = "baseline")
nt <- load_scores("peak-scores-nhsn-hindcasts.csv") |>
  filter(location != "US", season %in% c("2023/24", "2024/25"))
nt_dots <- function(map, metric, xlab, title, final) {
  d <- nt |> filter(model %in% names(map)) |> mutate(set = map[model], v = if (metric == "nls") -log_score else wis_log)
  s <- bind_rows(d |> group_by(set, season) |> summarise(v = mean(v), .groups = "drop"),
                 d |> group_by(set) |> summarise(v = mean(v)) |> mutate(season = "both")) |>
    mutate(season = factor(season, levels = c("2023/24", "2024/25", "both")))
  ord <- s |> filter(season == "both") |> arrange(desc(v)) |> pull(set)
  pos <- match(final, ord)
  ggplot(s, aes(v, factor(set, levels = ord))) + geom_blank() +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = pos - 0.45, ymax = pos + 0.45, fill = "#fde9df") +
    geom_point(aes(color = season, size = season == "both")) +
    scale_size_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 5, `FALSE` = 3), guide = "none") +
    scale_color_manual(NULL, values = c("2023/24" = "#e69f00", "2024/25" = "#56b4e9", "both" = INK)) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL, title = title)
}
(nt_dots(nt_tim, "nls", "peak-week −log score (lower is better)", "Timing", c("core", "core + holiday")) |
   nt_dots(nt_siz, "wis", "peak-size log-WIS (lower is better)", "Size", c("SB", "core"))) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

::: small
NHSN hindcasts, states, 2023/24 + 2024/25 (large dot: pooled). **Shaded: kept for the final models.** Timing: the full set is clearly worse; core and core + holiday tie. Size: all sets within noise; SB kept, with core as the simpler alternative. Final GBQR models pair them: size SB + timing core, and size core + timing core + holiday (next slides, with 2025/26 added).
:::

::: notes
Runs: N1 (size SB, timing core), N2 (size SB + lat/lon, timing core + holiday), N3 (size SB + B, timing core + B + lat/lon + recession + holiday), and core/core. Because size and timing are fitted separately, the timing scores of a run depend only on its timing set and the size scores only on its size set. These runs cover 2023/24 and 2024/25 only; 2025/26 was run only for the final models, which are in model-output (UMass-peak_gbqr_sb, UMass-peak_gbqr_core_hol). Source: analysis/peak-models/peak-scores-nhsn-hindcasts.csv.
:::

## NHSN: the three final models, by season

```{r f-nhsn-season}
#| fig-height: 6.6
um <- scores |> filter(model %in% names(MODEL_IDS), location != "US") |> mutate(label = factor(label, levels = unname(MODEL_IDS)))
by_season <- um |> group_by(label, season) |>
  summarise(`−log score` = -mean(log_score), RPS = mean(rps), `log-WIS` = mean(wis_log), .groups = "drop")
pt <- by_season |> pivot_longer(c(`−log score`, RPS)) |>
  ggplot(aes(season, value, fill = label)) + geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") + model_scale_fill(NULL, labels = TIMING_LABELS) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "lower is better", title = "Peak week (timing)") + guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))
ps <- ggplot(by_season, aes(season, `log-WIS`, fill = label)) + geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75) +
  model_scale_fill(NULL, labels = SIZE_LABELS) + labs(x = NULL, y = "log-WIS (lower is better)", title = "Peak size") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))
pt + ps + plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Real-time hindcasts, states (2023/24: 29 dates, 2024/25: 23, 2025/26: 28)",
                  caption = "Blue = UMass-peak_gbqr_sb (size SB, timing core) · orange = UMass-peak_gbqr_core_hol (size core, timing core + holiday)")
```

::: notes
Standardized scoring from model-output (UMass-peak_gbqr_sb, UMass-peak_gbqr_core_hol, UMass-peak_baseline), 52 locations without the US total. Each GBQR model has its own size and timing feature sets, so the legends name the set that produced the scores in each panel. Both GBQR models clearly beat the baseline in 2023/24 and 2025/26; in 2024/25 the baseline wins on peak size (log-WIS) and slightly on timing.
:::

## NHSN: where in the season the models win

```{r f-nhsn-wfp}
#| fig-height: 7.0
wf <- um |> filter(weeks_from_peak >= -10, weeks_from_peak <= 8) |>
  group_by(label, season, weeks_from_peak) |> summarise(`−log score` = -mean(log_score), `log-WIS` = mean(wis_log),
                                                        n = n(), .groups = "drop") |> filter(n >= 10)
wfp <- function(metric, labs_, ttl) {
  ggplot(wf, aes(weeks_from_peak, .data[[metric]], color = label)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#d9531e") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + facet_wrap(~season, nrow = 1) + model_scale_color(NULL, labels = labs_) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = metric, title = ttl) + theme(legend.position = "right")
}
(wfp("−log score", TIMING_LABELS, "Peak week: −log score") + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())) /
  (wfp("log-WIS", SIZE_LABELS, "Peak size: log-WIS") + labs(x = "forecast date minus observed peak week (weeks)")) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Scores by weeks from each state's peak (lower is better)")
```

## NHSN: calibration of peak size

```{r f-nhsn-cov}
#| fig-height: 6.6
cv <- bind_rows(um, um |> mutate(season = "all seasons")) |> group_by(label, season) |>
  summarise(`50% interval` = mean(cov50), `95% interval` = mean(cov95), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(c(`50% interval`, `95% interval`)) |>
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels = c("2023/24", "2024/25", "2025/26", "all seasons")))
ggplot(cv, aes(season, value, color = label)) + geom_blank() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.5, xmax = 4.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#f1f0ec") +
  geom_hline(data = tibble(name = c("50% interval", "95% interval"), t = c(0.5, 0.95)), aes(yintercept = t),
             linetype = "22", color = INK2) +
  geom_point(size = 5, position = position_dodge(0.5)) +
  geom_text(data = cv |> filter(season == "all seasons"), aes(label = percent(value, 1)),
            position = position_dodge(0.5), vjust = -1.1, size = 4.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~name) + model_scale_color(NULL, labels = SIZE_LABELS) +
  scale_y_continuous("coverage", labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(x = NULL, title = "Peak-size interval coverage by season and pooled over all three seasons (dashed: nominal)")
```

::: notes
`r ov <- um |> group_by(label) |> summarise(c50 = mean(cov50), c95 = mean(cov95)); paste0("Pooled over 2023/24–2025/26 (states, all forecast dates): ", paste0(SIZE_LABELS[as.character(ov$label)], " ", percent(ov$c50, 1), " (50%) / ", percent(ov$c95, 1), " (95%)", collapse = "; "), ".")` GBQR 50% intervals covered only 38–44% in 2023/24 and 2024/25 (too narrow) and about 75% in 2025/26 (too wide). Mean relative error of the median peak size: GBQR +21–28% in 2023/24, −21 to −23% in 2024/25 (record season), about +9% in 2025/26. The baseline over-predicted 2023/24 by 131% on average.
:::

## 2025/26: our models against the FluSight submissions

```{r f-hub-ours}
#| fig-height: 6.6
hs2 <- hs |> select(label, kind, all_of(H_NAMES[1:2]), n) |> pivot_longer(all_of(H_NAMES[1:2])) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, levels = H_NAMES[1:2]))
best <- hs |> arrange(`peak size: log-WIS`)
best_txt <- paste0("Lowest log-WIS: ", paste(best$label[1:3], f2(best$`peak size: log-WIS`[1:3], 3), collapse = "; "), ".")
best_rps <- hs |> arrange(`peak week: RPS`)
rps_txt <- paste0("Lowest RPS: ", paste(best_rps$label[1:4], f2(best_rps$`peak week: RPS`[1:4], 3), collapse = "; "), ".")
ggplot(hs2, aes(value, factor(label, levels = hub_order), fill = kind)) + geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_x") + model_scale_fill(NULL) +
  labs(x = "lower is better", y = NULL, title = "2025/26 peak forecasts, states — GBQR has the best peak-size log-WIS",
       caption = "GBQR SB / core: size SB, timing core · GBQR core / core+hol: size core, timing core + holiday")
```

::: notes
`r best_txt` `r rps_txt` Hub models are scored on their own submitted forecasts; ours are real-time hindcasts.
:::

## Takeaways

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
- **Size**: core + SB · **timing**: core (or core + holiday)
- **SB hurts timing** and **the baseline offset hurts size**, consistently
- Most exploratory gains (B share, lat/lon, recession, trend, H3) **did not carry over** to GBQR
- **2025/26**: GBQR best peak-size log-WIS of all FluSight submissions
- **2024/25**: the baseline beat GBQR — under-prediction in a record season, with under-reported latest weeks during the rise
- Next: diagnose 2024/25, GBQR + baseline ensemble, interval recalibration, seed sensitivity
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r f-takeaway}
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 6.2
tk <- um |> group_by(label) |> summarise(t = -mean(log_score), s = mean(wis_log))
tkp <- function(d, lab, ttl) ggplot(d, aes(v, factor(lab[as.character(label)], levels = rev(lab)), fill = label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) + geom_text(aes(x = v / 2, label = f2(v, 3)), color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5) +
  model_scale_fill(guide = "none") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = ttl)
tkp(tk |> mutate(v = t), TIMING_LABELS, "Peak week: −log score") /
  tkp(tk |> mutate(v = s), SIZE_LABELS, "Peak size: log-WIS") +
  plot_annotation(title = "NHSN 2023/24–2025/26, states", subtitle = "lower is better")
```
:::
:::

# Code and tools

## idmodels: the `idmodels.peak` subpackage

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: small
**Shared machinery**

- `base.py`: abstract **`PeakModel`** — `load_inputs(ref_date)` → **`PeakInputs`** (data, NHSN `vintages`, optional `strain` counts); `fit()` builds replay rows; `forecast()` / `run()` → hub CSV for both peak targets; **`CurrentSeason`**; subclasses implement `_fit(rows)` and `_predict(feats)` → (timing classes, z quantiles)
- `series.py`: **`SeasonArrays`**, `build_season_arrays`, `state_features` (core + SB; `SYNC_BURDEN_FEATURES`), `build_replay_rows`, `peak_week_climatology`
- `extra_features.py`: `FEATURE_GROUPS` = trend, recession, holiday, latlon, bshare, h3; `extra_features()`, `type_arrays()`, `holiday_matrix()`, `centroids()`
- `revision.py`: **`RevisionModel`** (block bootstrap of log revision ratios of the last 10 weeks, strata by count), `apply_revisions`, `load_nhsn_vintages`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: small
**`PeakModel` subclasses**

- **`PeakBaselineModel`** — conditional climatology
- **`PeakGBQRModel`** — LightGBM size quantiles + timing classes; separate `_size_features()` / `_timing_features()`; `oob_predict()`
- **`PeakKCDEModel`** — kernel conditional density / analogs
- **`PeakHierModel`** — Bayesian hierarchical (NumPyro) timing hazard + size
- **`PeakHybridModel`** (`PeakHierModel` subclass) — hierarchical model with GBQR out-of-bag predictions as offsets

KCDE, hierarchical and hybrid are implemented but not among the final models.
:::
:::
:::

## idmodels: configuration, commits and tests

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: small
**`config.py`**: abstract **`PeakModelConfig`** — `supplementary_sources` (ILINet, FluSurv-NET), `sync_burden_features`, `sync_reported_only`, `exclude_training_series`, `window_start_week` / `window_end_week` (10 / 43), `replay_start_week`, `min_window_obs`, `num_revision_draws` (200), `revision_max_lag` (10), `pmf_floor` (1e-4), `timing_smoothing_sd`, `num_size_levels`

- `PeakBaselineModelConfig` (`size_week_halfwidth`)
- **`PeakGBQRModelConfig`** (`num_bags` 25, `bag_frac_samples` 0.7, `max_k` 12, `size_offset`, **`size_feature_groups`**, **`timing_feature_groups`**, LightGBM `n_estimators`, `learning_rate`, `min_child_samples`)
- `PeakKCDEModelConfig`, `PeakHierModelConfig`, `PeakHybridModelConfig`

```python
PeakGBQRModelConfig(model_name="peak_gbqr_sb",
    size_feature_groups=["core", "sb"], timing_feature_groups=["core"])
PeakGBQRModelConfig(model_name="peak_gbqr_core_hol",
    size_feature_groups=["core"], timing_feature_groups=["core", "holiday"])
```
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: small
**Commits** (branch on reichlab/idmodels)

| commit | change |
|---|---|
| `bde15df` | direct seasonal peak models: base, baseline, GBQR, KCDE, revision, series |
| `8c56bf0` | hierarchical model, real-time validation hooks, new features |
| `1dd468d` | GBQR feature groups, `extra_features.py`, hybrid model |
| `da4f102` | influenza type counts through the NHSN path (`PeakInputs.strain`) |
| `f51b32c` | rename GBQR group `base` → `core` (alias kept) |

**Tests**: `tests/unit/peak/test_peak.py`, 21 tests — features and extra features never look ahead, replay targets, revision model, a valid hub submission from every model, GBQR out-of-bag predictions exclude their own season, size and timing feature sets are independent
:::
:::
:::
